pr_title: ddl: support column type change between decimal && SQL mode warnings
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: AilinKid <314806019@qq.com>

<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/19121

Since #19059 has supported the column type change between integers.

Linked Parser PR https://github.com/pingcap/parser/pull/1031

1. This PR is to support the column type change between decimal, for example, changing `decimal(5,2)` to `decimal(3,1)`.

2. This PR also tries to supply a kind of way to support the normal DDL warnings and strict DDL warnings which will be identified as warnings under non-strict SQL mode, otherwise, will be identified as errors. 

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

1: We have added the SQL Mode and warnings field in the parser. For why we don't put this into the job args directly, because the job args sometime will be cleaned at the end of `finishDDLJob`, and be substituted with delete range ids.

2: This PR only handled the SQL Mode and limited warning for column type change of decimal. There will be PRs later to complement the next works. For example, pass the SQL mode parameter to all DDL jobs and handle its warnings.

3: This PR only handled the column type between decimal, for more numeric types, such as float and double, more PRs is necessary.

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Integration test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- ddl: support column type change between decimal && SQL mode warnings

### Description

Supports transitions between the same types, including unsigned transitions.

### Value

- Support conversion between other Numeric types
    + Fixed-Point Types (Exact Value) - DECIMAL, NUMERIC
    + Floating-Point Types (Approximate Value) - FLOAT, DOUBLE
    + Bit-Value Type - BIT

review_comments: How about merge those 2 maps into 1 map?
good idea, how about refine this point in the next PR? (it needs an update in the parser and covers many code)

I found MySQL 5.7 reports the following notes instead:

```
mysql> show warnings;
+-------+------+----------------------------------------+
| Level | Code | Message                                |
+-------+------+----------------------------------------+
| Note  | 1265 | Data truncated for column 'a' at row 1 |
| Note  | 1265 | Data truncated for column 'a' at row 2 |
| Note  | 1265 | Data truncated for column 'a' at row 3 |
| Note  | 1265 | Data truncated for column 'a' at row 4 |
+-------+------+----------------------------------------+
4 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```
But it is not a big issue if the warning message is different.

yes, there 2 points to notice there.
1: The row count is not precious in the parallel reorganization.
2: Not all the specific datum value can be stored in the warning for each row, only the first row of one warning type with specific datum value does.

that means
```
Warning 1292 Truncated incorrect DECIMAL value: '111.22'
Warning 1292 Truncated incorrect DECIMAL value: '122.11' (won't be shown as  `value: '122.11'`, it will be seen as a copy the first one, because they are the same type)
```
So maybe the MySQL 5.7's warnings are more suitable for TiDB

IMHO it is better to rename `ReorgMeta` to something more general, say, something like `RuntimeCtx` since they're more like context at reorg runtime. What's more, `SQLMode` and `Warnings` may not only be needed by reorganization, other DDL jobs may need them as well.

`ReorgMeta` is an old struct defined in the parser. 
should we do this in another small pr to avoid another dependent pr waiting? I will also do it with Shuang's comment above.
Why we need to reset warnings here？
It's a partial result. After it was merged into the job, the next round DDL will collect new ones.
